skill.name: professional-communication
skill.description: Guide developers in writing clear professional messages, emails, meeting notes, status updates, and stakeholder communications.
skill.summary: Help developers communicate clearly across email, chat, meetings, and stakeholder updates.
skill.author: softaworks

remediation.suggestion: No security change is required, but future revisions can keep these terms inside explicit meeting or etiquette sections for clearer context.

content.value_statement: Software teams lose time when messages are unclear or aimed at the wrong audience. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code draft clear emails, chat updates, meeting notes, and stakeholder messages.
actual_capabilities: Structures professional emails with subject lines, context, requests, and next steps.
Improves team chat messages for clarity, channel fit, and async collaboration.
Creates meeting agendas, summaries, action items, and follow-up notes.
Adapts technical explanations for engineering peers, managers, customers, and non-technical stakeholders.
Provides reusable templates for status updates, escalations, follow-ups, and project delays.
Applies writing checks for active voice, scannable formatting, jargon reduction, and clear actions.
limitations: It provides communication guidance, not legal, human resources, or compliance advice.
It does not send messages, schedule meetings, or connect to email or chat systems.
It cannot verify facts, dates, names, or project status unless the user provides them.
It may need organization-specific tone, policy, or terminology supplied by the user.

use_cases.title: Write stakeholder updates
use_cases.description: Turn project status, risks, and next steps into concise updates for managers or business partners.

use_cases.title: Improve async team messages
use_cases.description: Convert vague chat messages into clear requests with context, urgency, and expected action.

use_cases.title: Prepare meeting communication
use_cases.description: Create agendas, decision summaries, and action-item follow-ups for planning, retrospectives, and design reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a clear email
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a structured message.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a professional email about [topic]. Include a clear subject, the main point first, brief context, the action needed, and a polite close.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite a chat message
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this team chat message so it is direct, async-friendly, and easy to answer: [paste message]. Keep the tone professional and concise.

prompt_templates.title: Create a meeting follow-up
prompt_templates.scenario: Summarize decisions and actions after a meeting.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a meeting follow-up for [meeting topic]. Use these notes: [paste notes]. Include key decisions, action items with owners, open questions, and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt for multiple audiences
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this technical update for three audiences: engineering peers, technical managers, and non-technical stakeholders. Preserve accuracy and adjust detail, tone, and jargon for each audience: [paste update].

output_examples.input: A developer needs to tell a manager that a release is delayed because QA found a payment bug.
output_examples.output:
Subject: Release Update: New Target Date Needed

The release needs to move by one week because QA found a payment issue that could affect customers. The team is fixing the bug now, QA will retest by Thursday, and I will share a confirmed launch date on Friday.

output_examples.input: A vague chat message says: “Hey, can I ask something about deploy?”
output_examples.output: Hi Sarah, quick question about the deployment script. I am seeing a permission error on line 42 during deploy. Have you seen this before, or should I open a support ticket?

output_examples.input: A design review ended with two decisions and three action items.
output: Key decisions: Use versioned endpoints. Keep the existing authentication flow for this release.
Action items: Priya updates the design doc by Wednesday. Marcus reviews error handling by Thursday. Alex schedules a follow-up if blockers remain.

best_practices: Lead with the main point, then add context and next steps.
Match detail, terminology, and tone to the audience receiving the message.
Use bullets, headings, owners, and dates when a message includes actions.
anti_patterns: Starting with vague greetings before stating the request.
Sending long blocks of text without structure or clear action items.
Using technical jargon with audiences who need business impact and plain language.

faq.question: Can this skill write emails for managers and stakeholders?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure status updates, requests, escalations, announcements, and follow-ups for professional audiences.

faq.question: Does it work for Slack, Teams, or Discord messages?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance applies to team chat tools and focuses on clear, async-friendly messages.

faq.question: Can it translate technical language for non-technical readers?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps preserve accuracy while reducing jargon and emphasizing business or customer impact.

faq.question: Does this skill send messages automatically?
faq.answer: No. It drafts and improves communication, but it does not connect to email, calendar, or chat services.

faq.question: What information should I provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide the audience, goal, context, deadline, facts to include, and any tone requirements.

faq.question: Is it suitable for sensitive workplace issues?
faq.answer: It can improve clarity and tone, but legal, human resources, or compliance issues need qualified review.
